facts.text: The applicant was born in 1954 and lives in Ankara.

facts.text: In the parliamentary elections of 3 November 2002, the applicant was elected MP for the Konya constituency to the Grand National Assembly of Turkey as a member of the People's Republican Party (CHP).

facts.text: Prior to his election he practised as a lawyer in Konya and two sets of criminal proceedings were brought against him: one for insulting a lawyer and the other for insulting a public official.

anchor.surface_text: 9.  Prior to his election he practised as a lawyer in Konya and, in the course of his professional activities, two sets of criminal proceedings were brought against him, one for insulting a lawyer and the other for insulting a public official.

facts.text: On 11 April 2003 the Konya Assize Court suspended the criminal proceedings against the applicant for insulting a public official by virtue of Article 83 of the Constitution and Article 253 § 4 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

anchor.surface_text: 13.  On 11 April 2003 the Konya Assize Court (“the Assize Court”) adopted a decision suspending the criminal proceedings against the applicant for insulting a public official, by virtue of Article 83 of the Constitution (on parliamentary immunity) and Article 253 § 4 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

facts.text: On 4 December 2003 the Assize Court transmitted the case file to the Ministry of Justice to have the applicant's parliamentary immunity lifted.

facts.text: On 28 May 2004 the joint committee decided to stay the proceedings against the applicant for insulting a public official until the end of his term of parliamentary office, noting that the applicant had requested the lifting of his immunity.

anchor.surface_text: 17.  On 28 May 2004, after noting that the applicant had requested the lifting of his immunity, the joint committee decided, in view of the nature of the charges, to stay the proceedings against him for insulting a public official until the end of his term of parliamentary office.

facts.text: The joint committee transmitted its decision to the plenary Assembly of the National Assembly.

facts.text: On 15 December 2004 the applicant challenged the joint committee's decision, arguing that parliamentary immunity was a relative and temporary privilege and should not be used to shield MPs from accountability.

facts.text: The examination of the matter of lifting the applicant's parliamentary immunity in the proceedings concerning insulting a lawyer was referred to the joint committee, which decided to stay the proceedings until the dissolution of the 22nd Parliament.

facts.text: During the 22nd Parliament's term two files concerned the applicant's immunity: one for insulting a lawyer and the other for insulting a public official; in both cases the joint committee decided to stay the proceedings until the end of his term of office.
